findings.title: Scanner-baseline cases pass on a ubs stand-in that drops the GitHub-permalink suffix real ubs appends to every detail line, so the rescue matches nothing on real output
findings.evidence: Compared fixture shape to the real tool. Real `ubs hooks/bead-capture-guard.py` run inside the repo prints detail lines as `    hooks/bead-capture-guard.py:305  Possible unreachable code after return — return None (https://github.com/craigvandotcom/agent-compounds/blob/eec40cff.../hooks/bead-capture-guard.py#L305)`. The same file content (git show 89dd650:...) scanned from a non-git scratch dir, which is how close-gate.sh:618 runs the baseline (`cd "$SCRATCH" && ubs ...`), prints the same lines with NO URL suffix. I piped both outputs through the gate's own sig_of awk (close-gate.sh:588): 5 HEAD signatures, 4 base signatures, 0 in common (`comm -12` gives 0). The signature carries the commit SHA and `#L<line>`, so it can never match a baseline, and the line number gets back in through the URL, which defeats the 'never by line number' design. The content-mode mock emits `$f:$ln:1  finding TOK present — rule.TOK` with no suffix, so AC4b Case A ('pre-existing ... rescued') passes 71/71. This matches the conductor's measurement on ac-4y7l.2: 0 pre-existing against a base where real ubs reports findings. It is the third epic-round instance of a hand-written stand-in for an external tool's output.
findings.fix: Replace the content-mode mock with the real shape: `path:line` with no column for python, plus a ` (https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/blob/<sha>/<path>#L<line>)` suffix when cwd is inside a git repo and none outside one. Better still, commit a captured real-ubs transcript as the fixture. The gate side then has to strip the trailing ` (https://...#L\d+)` in sig_of, or run the baseline from a context with the same shape. Add a case where HEAD runs in a git repo and base does not, and assert rescue > 0.

findings.title: Mock summary counters (all 0) contradict its own detail lines; real ubs lists fewer detail lines than it counts, so the SUM_TOTAL>HEAD_COUNT overflow always adds 'new' findings and no case exercises it
findings.evidence: Real ubs on hooks/bead-capture-guard.py prints `[info] ... (8 found)` but only 5 detail lines, and its Combined Summary says `Info: 8`. The same content scanned from the scratch dir gives Combined `Info: 16` (the per-scanner Info items are double-counted), still with only 5 detail lines. Under close-gate.sh:643, SUM_TOTAL(8) > HEAD_COUNT(5) therefore adds 3 unmatchable 'new' findings on every run, even if signature matching were fixed. The content mock hard-codes `Critical: 0 / Warning: 0 / Info: 0` next to N emitted findings, so SUM_TOTAL is always 0 and the overflow branch never runs in any AC4b case. Real python detail lines also have no `:col`, so the FINDINGS regex (`:[0-9]+:[0-9]+`) counts 0 on real output. The mock always adds `:1`, which hides this.
findings.fix: Make the mock's summary counters equal what real ubs reports: the count includes findings not listed as detail lines, and python lines have no column. Add a case where the base and HEAD both carry an identical truncated list ('8 found', 5 shown) and assert the gate does not refuse. On the gate side, compare the base summary counters against the HEAD summary counters for the overflow instead of comparing HEAD summary to HEAD detail count.

findings.title: refly.test.sh went red (18/2) when close-gate moved its landing record to --transition-comment; its br stub still ignores that flag
findings.evidence: Rerun at HEAD: `refly.test: 18 passed, 2 failed` (FAIL 'landed bead: no FRESH-VERIFY record', FAIL 'cascade bead: no TRIAGE-CLOSE record'). Same suite in a disposable worktree at 1ea8a59^: `20 passed, 0 failed`. Cause: 1ea8a59 removed close-gate's separate `comments add` and moved the record into `br close --transition-comment`. The refly stub's `close)` branch (line 194) only flips status and drops that argument, so nothing reaches BR_COMMENTS_LOG. close-gate.test.sh's own stub was updated for this change; this sibling harness was not. It stayed red through two later commits, so no gate runs it.
findings.fix: In refly.test.sh's stub `close)` branch, parse `--transition-comment <text>` and append it to "${BR_COMMENTS_LOG:?}", the same way close-gate.test.sh's mock does. Wire refly.test.sh into whatever gate runs close-gate.test.sh so a red sibling harness blocks the commit.

findings.title: Check-35 'identity by id, never position' case stays green when the fix is reverted to positional slicing
findings.evidence: Sabotage in a disposable worktree at 40140a5: I replaced `new_comments[rid] = [c for c in staged_comments if _comment_key(c) not in head_keys]` with the old `staged_comments[len(head_comments):]` in lint/checks/35-board-integrity.py. The whole suite still prints `OK: every board-integrity case passed`, including 'a legacy receipt sorted after a new comment is not re-judged (identity by id, never position)'. The fixture swaps the two legacy comments but appends the new id=13 LAST, so the positional slice staged[2:] gives exactly [id13] and reaches the same verdict. The case cannot tell identity from position. (The 'stale landing record' case does discriminate; it goes red under the rule-6 revert.)
findings.fix: Order the staged comments so position and identity disagree. Put the new canon comment BEFORE a legacy malformed one, e.g. staged [id13 (new, canon), id12, id11 (legacy, malformed)]. A positional slice then yields [id11] and false-FAILs, while identity yields [id13] and passes. Assert rc==0.
